A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same manifold-based GNN generalization study and contain readable main text, equations, proofs, experimental displays and appendices. Reformatting and localized typesetting defects do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original node-classification experiments on eight datasets and graph-classification/generalization experiments on ModelNet10 and ModelNet40, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark results and reports additional synthetic chair-manifold and spectral-regularization experiments.

M1.justification: v4 adds a spectral-continuity penalty to cross-entropy training, defined as R(h) = sum_k k|h_k|lambda_max^(k-1) in Eq. 108. This is a limited objective adaptation; the underlying GNN/MNN architectures, graph constructions and prediction procedures remain.

E1.justification: The eight real-world node datasets and ModelNet10/40 coverage remain. v4 adds a synthetic chair-manifold experiment, but does not clearly distinguish its data provenance from the sampled chair models already studied in v2. Whether this expands represented data/task coverage beyond a new experimental protocol is unclear.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate configurations of the same GNN/GCN family. v4's regularization-strength comparisons are sensitivity controls; no distinct baseline algorithm is added or removed.

E3.justification: v4 introduces fixed-weight synthetic sweeps and regularization-strength experiments. ModelNet10 changes from 3/4-layer GNNs with 10,20,...,80 training nodes to 2/3-layer GNNs with 20,40,...,100 nodes and regularization multipliers. The 100-node testing graph is retained. These substantially revise the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v4 adds direct sensitivity tests of spectral continuity and regularization, examining both generalization gaps and test accuracy (Figures 1 and 7). The ModelNet10 architecture-width comparison becomes a regularization-strength study (Figure 8), while the ModelNet40 architecture analysis remains in the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random partitions with means and standard deviations for graph experiments, ten independent runs for node experiments, and the same regression/Pearson estimation procedure. New uncertainty displays extend the existing reporting practice without documenting increased runs or new statistical tests.

E6.justification: New curves show dependence on spectral continuity and reduced test accuracy under excessive regularization (v4 Figures 1 and 7). ModelNet10 output-difference curves are replaced under changed settings, so they are not same-setting performance gains. Table 1, all 92 numerical rows in Tables 3–10, and the ModelNet40 results are retained.

T1.justification: Most explicit C_L dependence is an equivalent expansion of constants already defined in v2 Appendix B. v4 additionally defines R(h) in Eq. 108 and changes coefficient placement in Theorem 2: Eq. 18 multiplies the sampling-error term by C1 C_L+C2, unlike v2 Eq. 19 and v4's proof Eq. 102. Most assumptions and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes generalization improving with graph size for node- and graph-level tasks. v4 adds headline contributions concerning linear dependence on spectral continuity and a discriminability–generalization trade-off, including the claim that restricting discriminability is necessary for better generalization. These materially expand the abstract, introduction and conclusion claims.

C2.justification: v4 develops a substantive mechanism interpretation: smoother filters reduce the generalization bound but discriminate fewer spectral components, potentially increasing training loss and harming test accuracy. It discusses balancing these effects and explains excessive regularization as a failure condition. v2's discussion primarily concerned graph size, manifold dimension and architecture size.

D1.justification: v4 provides the implementable spectral-regularizer formula, defines its largest-eigenvalue dependence and displays tested multipliers. Existing hardware, optimizers, training budgets, dropout, dataset-loading instructions and data-source links are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds explicit contrasts with prior bounds that grow with node count, degree or maximum eigenvalue. The cited works are retained; the manifold-learning references appearing in the main related-work section were already discussed in v2 Appendix G.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theorem interpretations, conclusion and appendix discussion are extensively rewritten. The introductory informal theorem is removed, a four-part contribution list is added, and manifold-learning discussion moves into Related works. Section and appendix numbering disappears, leaving several incomplete internal references.

P2.justification: v4 substantially restyles the title block and page layout, replaces the opening Arxiv summary with a synthetic figure, adds a filter schematic and regularization plots, and redraws ModelNet10 results with shaded uncertainty. Retained tables and figures are resized and relocated. Some dataset-loading commands now extend beyond the page edge.

improvement.justification: v4 directly tests spectral smoothness and demonstrates that smaller generalization gaps can coexist with worse test accuracy, making the practical implications more informative than in v2. This is a modest net gain in empirical support and interpretation. The improvement is limited by the new Eq. 18/proof Eq. 102 coefficient inconsistency, incomplete appendix references and clipped dataset-loading commands.
